page: Microsoft Azure L48s_v4 is a storage-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capabilities are defined by a massive 11,519 GB local NVMe SSD, making it highly suitable for applications requiring high-throughput, low-latency local storage. It is also Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance across several domains. The memory subsystem demonstrates high bandwidth, reaching 3700.79 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 223.94 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Computational benchmarks show a Passmark CPU score of 63,100.84 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,273.0. Database operations are highly efficient, with Redis SET operations achieving 67.33 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 25,789.77.

Given its high local storage capacity and strong memory bandwidth, the L48s_v4 offers high resource density for data-intensive workloads. It is highly optimized for large-scale databases, big data analytics, caching layers, and high-throughput web serving. The inclusion of AMX instructions also supports CPU-based machine learning inference, as evidenced by strong prompt processing speeds in LLM benchmarks.
description: Microsoft Azure L48s_v4 is a storage-optimized server instance designed for high-throughput, data-intensive workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, it delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs, 24 physical cores, and a 260 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 384.0 GB of RAM and a massive 11,519 GB local NVMe SSD, providing exceptional local storage capacity and a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Performance benchmarks highlight strong capabilities, including a Passmark CPU score of 63,100.84, a Redis SET throughput of 67.33 million operations per second, and high memory read bandwidth of 223.94 GB/sec for large blocks. Lacking a GPU, it relies on Intel AMX instructions to accelerate CPU-based vector and matrix calculations. This hardware profile makes the L48s_v4 highly efficient for large databases, caching layers, and high-throughput web serving.
